title: Air India Overhauls Mobile App With In-House Booking Engine, AI Tools and India-Specific Payments
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier's revamped app now handles bookings directly, offers UPI and Indian payment options, and provides AI-assisted flight disruption support for its 100,000 daily users.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India launches overhauled mobile app with in-house booking engine and proprietary payment platform
  • App serves over 100,000 daily users and has been downloaded 17 million times
  • New payment orchestration system supports UPI and India-specific innovations
  • Flight disruption tools now offer hotel and transport assistance from the home screen
  • Part of Tata Group's broader digital transformation since acquiring the airline in 2022
Air India on Thursday rolled out a major overhaul of its mobile application, bringing in-house booking capabilities, a proprietary payment platform and expanded disruption-assistance tools to an app that now serves over 100,000 users daily. ## What's New The most significant change is structural: Air India's app now runs its own booking engine instead of acting as a front-end for third-party systems. This means the airline controls the full transaction — from fare display to ticket issuance — allowing for faster performance and more flexibility. The second major addition is a proprietary payment orchestration system, which Chief Digital and Technology Officer Satya Ramaswamy described as a platform for deploying India-specific payment innovations quickly. "Payment orchestration system allows us to do a lot of India-specific innovations. It will allow us to deploy the innovations quickly," Ramaswamy told PTI. The practical upshot: support for UPI and other Indian payment methods that many diaspora travellers use when booking flights, with the ability to add new options as they emerge. ## Disruption Assistance For travellers — and anyone who has experienced the frustration of an Air India delay or cancellation — the app now surfaces hotel accommodation and transportation assistance contextually from the home screen when flights are disrupted. This replaces the previous process of calling customer service or visiting a counter. ## Part of a Larger Transformation The app has been downloaded nearly 17 million times, reflecting Air India's reach among India's travelling public and the global diaspora. Since the Tata Group acquired the loss-making carrier from the government in January 2022, it has modernised more than 140 digital systems as part of an ambitious transformation plan. The revamped app sits alongside Air India's earlier AI-driven innovations, including the "eZ Booking" feature that uses agentic AI to let Maharaja Club loyalty members complete reservations through text or voice commands. ## Why It Matters for the Diaspora Air India remains the primary carrier connecting India to its global diaspora, operating routes to North America, Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Australia. For NRI travellers who book trips home regularly, an app that actually works — with Indian payment options, faster booking and automatic disruption handling — addresses long-standing pain points. Under the Tata Group's stewardship, Air India has been steadily closing the technology gap with Gulf and East Asian carriers. The app overhaul is the most visible sign yet that the airline's digital transformation is reaching the customer-facing layer where it matters most.
